observations.why: The declarative 'we are adopting' enacts a decisional authority — the speaker commits the collective to a choice, performing rank-based allocation rather than proposing or negotiating.
The proportional cost-benefit comparison ('15x faster than our current setup') frames the decision in proportionality terms — a market-pricing justification for the adoption.
Stating when the migration starts enacts scheduling authority — the speaker sets a timeline the organization is expected to follow, a rank-based allocation of time and resources.
The summary re-presents the adoption through a proportionality lens — quantified performance gain as the rationale, a market-pricing framing of the decision.
